extracted.intended_audience: authors/researchers reporting observational epidemiologic studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional); journal editors and reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: A checklist of items that should be included when reporting observational studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional), covering title/abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, and other information to ensure transparent reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract
rubrics_metrics.description:
(a) Indicate the study’s design with a commonly used term in the title or the abstract

(b) Provide in the abstract an informative and balanced summary of what was done and what was found
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a commonly understood design term (e.g., 'cohort study', 'case-control study', 'cross-sectional study') in title/abstract. The abstract should be informative and balanced, summarising methods and main findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background/rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the scientific background and rationale for the investigation being reported
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State why the study was done and the knowledge gap it addresses; give context that justifies the study design and choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: State specific objectives, including any prespecified hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give clear, specific objectives and any hypotheses that were defined before data analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design
rubrics_metrics.description: Present key elements of study design early in the paper
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the observational design (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) and the main design features up front so readers understand the study structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the setting, locations, and relevant dates, including periods of recruitment, exposure, follow-up, and data collection
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give geographic and institutional context and explicit timing (dates and periods) for recruitment, exposures, follow-up, and when data were collected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants — eligibility and selection
rubrics_metrics.description:
(a) Cohort study—Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of selection of participants. Describe methods of follow-up

Case-control study—Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of case ascertainment and control selection. Give the rationale for the choice of cases and controls

Cross-sectional study—Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of selection of participants
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report who was eligible, how participants were identified and recruited, and rationale for selection methods. For cohort studies include follow-up methods; for case-control studies justify control selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants — matching
rubrics_metrics.description:
(b) Cohort study—For matched studies, give matching criteria and number of exposed and unexposed

Case-control study—For matched studies, give matching criteria and the number of controls per case
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When matching was used, state the matching variables and the numbers in matched groups (e.g., exposed/unexposed or controls per case).

rubrics_metrics.name: Variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define all outcomes, exposures, predictors, potential confounders, and effect modifiers. Give diagnostic criteria, if applicable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise definitions and, where relevant, diagnostic or case definitions to allow reproducibility and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources/measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: For each variable of interest, give sources of data and details of methods of assessment (measurement). Describe comparability of assessment methods if there is more than one group
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State how each variable was measured and the data source (e.g., interviews, records, laboratory). If different groups had different assessment methods describe comparability and any harmonisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any efforts to address potential sources of bias
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe methods used to reduce or assess potential biases (selection, information, measurement, confounding), including design or analytical steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study size
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the study size was arrived at
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sample size considerations, including any power/sample size calculations, practical constraints, or rationale for chosen size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how quantitative variables were handled in the analyses. If applicable, describe which groupings were chosen and why
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether continuous variables were used as continuous or categorised, and justify cutpoints or groupings; describe transformations if used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description:
(a) Describe all statistical methods, including those used to control for confounding

(b) Describe any methods used to examine subgroups and interactions

(c) Explain how missing data were addressed

(d) Cohort study—If applicable, explain how loss to follow-up was addressed

Case-control study—If applicable, explain how matching of cases and controls was addressed

Cross-sectional study—If applicable, describe analytical methods taking account of sampling strategy

(e) Describe any sensitivity analyses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full detail on the analytical approach: modelling methods, confounder control (e.g., adjustment variables), subgroup/interaction testing, handling of missing data (imputation, exclusions), and sensitivity analyses. For design-specific issues (loss to follow-up, matching, sampling) describe how these were handled analytically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants — numbers at each stage
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Report numbers of individuals at each stage of study—eg numbers potentially eligible, examined for eligibility, confirmed eligible, included in the study, completing follow-up, and analysed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give counts at each important stage; consider using a flow diagram to illustrate participant flow through the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants — reasons for non-participation and flow diagram
rubrics_metrics.description:
(b) Give reasons for non-participation at each stage

(c) Consider use of a flow diagram
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report why participants were not included or lost and consider a flowchart to make the process transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive data
rubrics_metrics.description:
(a) Give characteristics of study participants (eg demographic, clinical, social) and information on exposures and potential confounders

(b) Indicate number of participants with missing data for each variable of interest

(c) Cohort study—Summarise follow-up time (eg, average and total amount)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide baseline/descriptive tables with participant characteristics, exposure and confounder distributions, and counts of missing data. For cohort studies report follow-up duration (mean, total person-time).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome data
rubrics_metrics.description:
Cohort study—Report numbers of outcome events or summary measures over time

Case-control study—Report numbers in each exposure category, or summary measures of exposure

Cross-sectional study—Report numbers of outcome events or summary measures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the primary outcome event counts or summary statistics appropriate to the design so readers can assess the occurrence and distribution of outcomes/exposures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main results
rubrics_metrics.description:
(a) Give unadjusted estimates and, if applicable, confounder-adjusted estimates and their precision (eg, 95% confidence interval). Make clear which confounders were adjusted for and why they were included

(b) Report category boundaries when continuous variables were categorized

(c) If relevant, consider translating estimates of relative risk into absolute risk for a meaningful time period
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present both crude and adjusted effect estimates with measures of precision; explicitly state adjustment sets. When categorising continuous variables, state the cutpoints. Translate relative measures into absolute risks when helpful for interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Report other analyses done—eg analyses of subgroups and interactions, and sensitivity analyses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report results of secondary and exploratory analyses (subgroups, interactions, sensitivity checks) and indicate whether these were prespecified or post hoc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key results
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarise key results with reference to study objectives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin the discussion with a concise summary linking main findings back to the stated objectives/hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss limitations of the study, taking into account sources of potential bias or imprecision. Discuss both direction and magnitude of any potential bias
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge study weaknesses, likely biases, measurement error, residual confounding, and discuss how these might affect the direction and magnitude of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a cautious overall interpretation of results considering objectives, limitations, multiplicity of analyses, results from similar studies, and other relevant evidence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret findings in light of study limitations, consistency with other evidence, and the potential for chance due to multiple analyses; avoid overstating conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the generalisability (external validity) of the study results
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider to which populations and settings the results might apply, and what limits generalisability (sampling, selection, setting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the source of funding and the role of the funders for the present study and, if applicable, for the original study on which the present article is based
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose funding sources and describe any influence funders had on design, analysis, interpretation, or reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate reporting for study groups (footnote)
rubrics_metrics.description: *Give information separately for cases and controls in case-control studies and, if applicable, for exposed and unexposed groups in cohort and cross-sectional studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where relevant, present tables and results stratified by study groups (cases/controls, exposed/unexposed) so differences between groups are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation and Elaboration resource
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: An Explanation and Elaboration article discusses each checklist item and gives methodological background and published examples of transparent reporting. The STROBE checklist is best used in conjunction with this article (freely available on the Web sites of PLoS Medicine, Annals of Internal Medicine, and Epidemiology). Information on the STROBE Initiative is available at www.strobe-statement.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Explanation and Elaboration article for methodological background and example reporting; the checklist is intended to be used alongside that explanatory material.
